title: Email to Telegram – Operations
description: Is mail getting from the sender to Telegram, how fast, and where is it lost.

list.name: App start
list.expr: (max by (instance, env, version) (process_start_time_seconds{job=~"email_to_telegram_(staging|prod)",env=~"$env"} * on (instance, job) group_left (version) email_to_telegram_build_info{env=~"$env"}) * 1000) or on (instance, env) (max by (instance, env) (process_start_time_seconds{job=~"email_to_telegram_(staging|prod)",env=~"$env"}) * 1000)

panels.title: Scrape up
panels.description: Prometheus reaches the app's /metrics. DOWN: the app or its metrics endpoint is unreachable, and every other panel goes stale.

panels.title: Version
panels.description: App version the selected env runs (email_to_telegram_build_info). unknown: the running app predates that metric.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the app process started. Blue markers on the time series are process starts (deploys or crashes); a restart without a deploy is the bad case.

panels.title: Stale bot updates (24h)
panels.description: Telegram text messages the bot skipped because they were older than STALE_TEXT_UPDATE_MAX_AGE_S (default 10 min) when it got them: a backlog after an outage or a long restart. The user has to send them again. Button taps, membership changes and chat-migration messages are never skipped. Two values: the 24-h increase, and the highest total one process reported in 24 h. Skips happen right after a start, often before the first 30-s scrape, so the increase can miss them (the first sample is already non-zero); the process total catches those that a later scrape still sees, but a process that stops before its first scrape is missed by both. Exact count: the telegram.update.stale_skipped log lines in Loki, sum(count_over_time({compose_project="email-to-telegram", service="app", env="$env"} |= "telegram.update.stale_skipped" [24h])). Bad: a non-zero count without a long outage to explain it.

panels.title: Offered (24h)
panels.description: Mail offered: preflight checks the Worker ran in the last 24 h, accepted + bounced + deferred (a deferred mail is offered again on each retry). Signature failures excluded. Orange at 0: no mail reached the app for a day.

panels.title: Delivered (24h)
panels.description: Mails Telegram accepted in the last 24 h, first attempts plus retries. Compare with Mail offered: a large gap means mail is bounced, deferred or failing.

panels.title: Lost (7d)
panels.description: Mail closed as permanently failed in 7 days, so the user never got it: a first attempt to a blocked or deleted chat, a retry that ran out of budget, or a raw email that expired before delivery. Red above 0; the Delivery row splits it by stage.

panels.title: Backlog now
panels.description: Delivery logs not delivered or closed yet, and the age of the oldest. A few seconds is normal; the retry worker runs every 5 min. Orange past 10 min, red past 1 h: mail is stuck.

panels.title: Latency (24h)
panels.description: Delivery p95: 95th percentile of receive-to-Telegram time over 24 h. Seconds is normal; orange past 1 min (mail going through the retry worker), red past 15 min.

panels.title: Preflight decisions per hour
panels.description: What the Worker asked before taking a mail. accepted: uploaded next; deferred: 429 over the alias hourly cap, the sender retries later (not a loss); bounced: refused with a permanent 550. Bad: bounced dominating, or nothing accepted while mail is expected.

panels.title: Preflight bounces by reason per hour
panels.description: Why preflight refused mail (the sender gets a permanent bounce). monthly_email_limit: a user over the monthly cap; sender_not_allowed: an alias with no allow rules; alias_not_found: unknown address. Older data also counts hourly-cap deferrals here as rate_limited.

panels.title: Raw uploads per hour
panels.description: Mail the Worker uploaded after preflight accepted it. accepted: stored and queued for delivery. Bad: rejected climbing, or nothing accepted while preflight accepts (the Worker to app contract is broken).

panels.title: Raw rejections by reason per hour
panels.description: Why an uploaded mail was not queued. sender_not_allowed / sender_auth_failed: failed the alias allow rules; duplicate: already received. rate_limited (kept for recovery) and sender_auth_temperror (503, the sender retries) are not losses. Any *_signature reason: the Worker and app disagree on the signing secret or version.

panels.title: Bounce notices per hour by result
panels.description: Messages telling the owner of a not-yet-working alias that mail bounced because no allow rule matched (raw stage: rules exist but none matched; preflight: the alias has no rules). sent: Telegram accepted it. gated: the alias already delivered, is not active, or is older than 7 days with an owner who had mail accepted. not_claimed: the 24 h window or the 3-notice budget of that alias. dropped: the bounded queue was full, or a deadline or shutdown stopped the job. stale: the alias or its claim changed before the send. failed: a DB or Telegram error. Bad: failed or dropped climbing.

defaults.noValue: No bounce notices in this range

panels.title: One-tap allows per hour by result
panels.description: Taps on "Allow <domain>" in a bounce notice. added: the rule exists now. expired: the button was spent, replaced by a newer notice, older than 7 days, or the alias moved, paused or was deleted. failed: the rule limit or a DB error (the button is spent). Read with the sent notices next to it: added over sent is the share of notices that ended in a rule.

panels.title: Deliveries per hour
panels.description: Telegram sends by path and result. A failed first attempt goes to the retry worker; retry permanently_failed gave up (see Lost mail). Bad: failures rising while successes drop.

panels.title: Lost mail per hour by stage
panels.description: Mail closed as permanently failed, so the user never got it. initial: first attempt to a blocked or deleted chat; retry: the retry worker gave up; cleanup: the raw email expired before any delivery succeeded. Bad: any bar, and cleanup bars most of all (Telegram was unreachable for the whole raw-email TTL).

defaults.noValue: No lost mail in this range

panels.title: Delivery latency p50 / p95 (1h window)
panels.description: Time from receiving a mail to Telegram accepting its first message, over a sliding hour (log scale). A few seconds is normal; minutes mean mail went through the retry worker. Gaps: no deliveries in that hour.

panels.title: First-attempt success rate per hour
panels.description: Share of first delivery attempts Telegram accepted in each hour. A missing bar means no attempts that hour (idle, not failure). Bad: bars below ~95%, or several short ones in a row.

defaults.noValue: No first attempts in this range

panels.title: Delivery backlog
panels.description: Delivery logs not in a final state, by status (stacked), and the oldest one's age (dashed, right axis). received / processing clear in seconds; failed / retrying wait for the retry worker. Bad: a count or age that keeps growing.

panels.title: Telegram send failures per hour by class
panels.description: Failed Telegram sends (first attempts, retries, attachment fallbacks). forbidden / chat_not_found: the user blocked the bot or deleted the chat; flood_wait / timeout / network / server: Telegram side, retried; bad_request: a message Telegram refuses. Bad: any class climbing.

defaults.noValue: No send failures in this range

panels.title: Rich vs classic fallback per hour
panels.description: Messages that carry rich formatting (not every mail does). success: sent rich; fallback: Telegram refused the rich message and the classic one went out; disabled: rich messages are off or unavailable. Bad: fallback rising against success.

panels.title: Backpressure: sent to retry worker (24h)
panels.description: Accepted mail handed straight to the retry worker because MAX_INFLIGHT_DELIVERIES was reached. Not the preflight deferral (that mail never reached the app); it is still delivered, minutes later. Bad: a steady non-zero count.

panels.title: Backpressure per hour
panels.description: Same signal per hour: mail queued past the in-flight delivery cap and left for the retry worker. Bad: bursts that line up with latency spikes.

panels.title: Local rich downgrades per hour by reason
panels.description: Classic messages sent because the body hit a rich limit (not privacy mode, not the rich switch, not a Telegram rejection: that is fallback above). Reason is the first limit hit: input_limit, text_limit, block_limit, column_limit, depth_limit; delivery_budget: the header or attachments tipped it over. Counted per acknowledged send, so a resend counts again. Read it against success above: the share of rich-eligible mail that went classic locally.

panels.title: Requests per hour by status class
panels.description: All app routes except /healthz and /metrics (probe and scrape traffic). 4xx on the unknown route is internet scanning. Bad: any 5xx.

panels.title: Requests per hour by route
panels.description: Same traffic split by route, probes excluded. /inbound/preflight and /inbound/raw track mail volume; unknown is unmatched paths (scanners). Bad: a route that should be busy dropping to zero.

panels.title: p95 latency by route (1h window)
panels.description: 95th percentile request time per route over a sliding hour, probes excluded. /inbound/raw includes storing the mail. Bad: seconds on /inbound/preflight, the Worker waits on it while the sender is connected.

panels.title: Prod app lines (15 min)
panels.description: Lines from the prod app container that reached Loki in the last 15 minutes, whatever Env is set to. 0 while prod is handling mail means prod logs are not arriving: the prod log collector is down, the push gateway refuses it, or prod runs a release from before the app's logging labels. A quiet app can also log nothing for 15 minutes.

panels.title: App error logs
panels.description: Pino error and fatal lines from the app container of the selected env (Loki). Both environments ship the app container only: staging through its local collector, prod through the push gateway. Bad: anything here.

panels.title: Disk free (/)
panels.description: Free space on the root filesystem (node_exporter). Orange under 20%, red under 10%: attachments, raw mail and backups soon stop being written.

panels.title: RAM available
panels.description: MemAvailable on the host. Orange under 500 MB, red under 200 MB: the kernel starts killing processes.

panels.title: Load (1m)
panels.description: 1-minute load average. Bad: above the host's CPU count for a long stretch.

panels.title: Swap used
panels.description: Swap in use on the host. Bad: steadily growing, the host is short of memory.

panels.title: Postgres up
panels.description: postgres_exporter can query the database. DOWN: the database is unreachable and the app cannot accept or deliver mail.

panels.title: DB connections
panels.description: Backends connected to the emailtelegram database. Bad: near the server's max_connections, new queries start failing.

panels.title: DB size
panels.description: On-disk size of the emailtelegram database. Bad: fast growth (retention jobs not running).

panels.title: Backup age
panels.description: Time since the last successful off-site backup (node_exporter textfile collector). Red over 30 h: a nightly run failed.

panels.title: Root filesystem free (%)
panels.description: Free space on / over time. Bad: a steady downward slope; extrapolate it to see when the disk fills.

panels.title: Memory available
panels.description: MemAvailable over time. Bad: a downward trend that does not recover (a leak) or dips under ~200 MB.

panels.title: Load (1m)
panels.description: 1-minute load average over time. Bad: long stretches above the CPU count.
